sections.value:
**Performance: BLOCK P175-F001 / P175-F002** at `59950a5ef6334faa57a57f35f178b284354287e1`.

Whole-PR review against main `c2c8b1c9`. No earlier #175 verdict was published; all earlier heads were held.

**P175-F001: build-only stamps escape into the running daemon and background Cargo builds.** Both justfile recipes `export PIJ_BUILD_COMMIT`, `PIJ_EXT_TREE_COPILOT` and `PIJ_EXT_TREE_OMP`. In `bounce-rs`, those exports remain when the later `nohup ... daemon` runs. They are not consumed/unset at daemon startup.

The existing background launcher (`crates/daemon/src/background.rs:399-425`) inherits the daemon environment, and its runner executes `/bin/sh -c "$PIJ_BG_COMMAND"` without clearing these variables (`:184-205`). Therefore a background Cargo command in another worktree, without explicitly setting any stamp, receives the **production checkout's** stamps. It can compile an unrelated worktree's daemon with a wrong commit/expected-extension identity and acquire environment-dependent cache misses on subsequent builds. This contradicts the stated fallback that other build methods are unstamped. I am not claiming all tmux seats inherit them; this concrete background-job path does.

**Required:** scope stamp variables to the Cargo build invocation, or remove them before launching the runtime daemon. Preserve the baked-in constants for the intended production build, but do not leak their build inputs into runtime descendants. Add fake build/runtime-child environment proof without a real bounce or compiler run.

**P175-F002: the advertised bounded tree parse allocates before enforcing its bound.** `reported_tree` collects every `text.split('+')` item into `Vec<&str>`, then checks for 1-4 IDs. Accepted grammar length is bounded; malformed input's intermediate vector is not bounded by that grammar. Stored `extension_build` is read as an unrestricted String, so separators can amplify transient allocation on each digest row before the value is discarded. Daemon stamps are also reparsed per matching row.

**Required:** reject oversized tree text or use a bounded split before collection, enforcing the maximum four IDs/40 bytes each without a delimiter-proportional vector. Keep existing malformed-value behavior and grammar tests. The preceding `split_once(" tree:")` and an invalid build prefix's `chars().count()` remain linear in raw text; price or bound that input work honestly rather than calling the entire operation constant/bounded by the accepted IDs.

**Runtime shape checked:** the stale check runs when an existing PA digest is constructed (idle-edge, prime-active or dormant wake), on its existing seat rows. It adds no registry/spine read, process probe, timer or executable site. It parses the daemon tree and reported tree, compares them, and only on mismatch parses the build prefix/constructs an anomaly. Healthy same-tree rows still pay parse/allocation; Claude/Codex, unstamped or no-tree cases skip comparison. F127's other unsafe digest fields remain outside this review.

**Load cost:** Copilot computes its identity once before its re-registration loop; OMP keeps it in a module-level constant. Registration retries/status updates reuse it. Healthy Git-backed loads retain two existing calls: combined HEAD/tree rev-parse and scoped status. OMP's new retry occurs on **any first rev-parse exception**, not only a missing outside file; it can make three calls if the retry and status succeed, or two failed attempts before hash fallback. Both helpers retain their existing two-second timeout settings; OMP's synchronous timeout is not an unconditional wall-time cap. Hash fallbacks retain in-process source reads. No new per-tick Git call.

**Build/cache answer:** one Git rev-parse returns HEAD plus the two directory trees and OMP outside blob. The recipes also perform four `$(printf ...)` command-substitution subshell evaluations to shorten those values; the “one Git” row is not a complete subprocess-work budget. Prefer shell-native formatting where practical.

Tree comparison avoids stale alerts after outside-scope docs/daemon changes, **but it does not eliminate docs-only compilation**: `PIJ_BUILD_COMMIT` still changes at every HEAD and is `option_env!` in the daemon library, alongside the two tree stamps. [Cargo automatically tracks env!/option_env! changes](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html#rerun-if-env-changed), so a changed/set/unset value rebuilds the affected daemon unit and applicable dependents. CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 disables incremental compilation, not Cargo's whole-unit up-to-date cache; it does not make this tax disappear.

This is **not a global cache flush**. Independent target directories/profiles are not directly invalidated. Default debug tests do not overwrite release artifacts merely by omitting stamps; same-profile/shared-unit stamped-to-unstamped builds can recompile. Unrelated dependency crates do not reference these keys. Shared-build already touches workspace lib/main sources on each hold, independently forcing workspace freshness; the direct install/bounce recipes do not use that refresh. A small metadata/CLI compilation boundary would contain the full-HEAD stamp's rebuild fan-out better, but no local cache-timing experiment was run.

**Closure sensor:** it is a test-only filesystem walk, not runtime work or a Git launch. Each reachable source is read once through the seen set; quoted-relative scanning makes six passes and performs candidate-file metadata lookups. The new escape checks add normalization/comparisons and one scratch-fixture case. The five authored escape forms and real-tree probes are covered as stated; paths assembled without an escaping literal remain the declared lexical limit.

**CI:** [42447684985](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42447684985) succeeds at this exact SHA. The latest successful Rust job identifies **artifact13604179945**, not the older same-name artifact: **2,206 executed cases passed**, with five separately skipped. Verified grammar/hostile-text tests, all three closure cases and six spawn guards. Node22/24 each execute **14 OMP identity tests**; Node22's native suite reports 330 passed. These do not test runtime stamp-env isolation or bounded malformed-tree allocation. Delivers `42447699011` succeeds.

Worktree and GitHub heads agree; clean and CLEAN/MERGEABLE. No local Cargo, build, test, mutation, load probe or daemon restart. The blockers concern stamp scope and parser work, not the already-reviewed escaping-path security grammar.
